ir4_programme.topic: Iran's nuclear programme, 1957–2026: origins, revelations, IAEA findings, enrichment, NPT status, fatwa

claims.text: Eisenhower's Atoms for Peace speech to the UN General Assembly, 8 Dec 1953; US–Iran civil nuclear cooperation agreement 1957; in 1967 the US supplied a 5-MW research reactor and HEU fuel; in 1974 the Shah announced 20 reactors in 20 years; in 1976 AEOI budget rose from $31m to $1bn

Tehran Research Reactor (5 MW, US-supplied) went critical Nov 1967, initially on ~93% HEU, converted to 20% fuel in 1993; Iran's parliament ratified the NPT Feb 1970; 1974 AEOI founded with plans for ~23,000 MW; 1979 revolution halted projects; 1987 Iran acquired P-1 centrifuge schematics from the A.Q. Khan network; Aug 2002 NCRI disclosed Natanz and Arak; 21 Oct 2003 Iran agreed with EU foreign ministers to suspend enrichment and sign Additional Protocol; 24 Sep 2005 IAEA Board found non-compliance 22-1-12; 4 Feb 2006 referral to UNSC; UNSC 1696 (31 Jul 2006), 1737 (23 Dec 2006), 1747, 1803, 1929 (9 Jun 2010); 8 Nov 2011 IAEA report on structured programme prior to 2004; JPOA 24 Nov 2013; JCPOA 14 Jul 2015; 2 Dec 2015 assessment; 16 Jan 2016 implementation day; 1 Jul 2019 exceeded 300 kg; 7–8 Jul 2019 ~4.5% enrichment

Iran signed the NPT July 1968; in force for Iran 5 Mar 1970; 1974 Shah lent $1bn to France's Eurodif, Kraftwerk Union began Bushehr; 1979 programme frozen and Bushehr contract terminated; Jan 1995 $800m contract with Russia to complete Bushehr; IAEA 11 Nov 2003 report found breaches and a 'policy of concealment' but 'no evidence' of a bomb attempt; 8 Nov 2011 report on possible military dimensions, Parchin high-explosive testing

NSDM 292 (22 Apr 1975, Kissinger): US would approve reprocessing in Iran under multinational/binational arrangement; July 1975 embassy assessment found the Shah's motives 'Not Entirely Clear', possibly keeping a nuclear option; agreement initialed 1978 but never signed, nullified by revolution

14 Aug 2002, Alireza Jafarzadeh for the NCRI, Washington press conference: Natanz site near Kashan under cover of a desert-eradication project via front company Kala-Electric; Arak heavy-water project via Mesbah Energy; findings credited to PMOI
Gerami and Goldschmidt: US reportedly briefed the IAEA nearly three months before the NCRI press conference; IAEA took more than two years to reach formal non-compliance

IAEA GOV/2011/65 annex (8 Nov 2011): information 'consistent in terms of technical content, individuals and organizations involved, and time frames'; AMAD plan under Fakhrizadeh before end 2003; Iran 'might be continuing to pursue some of the activities'; Parchin containment chamber; neutron initiator; Shahab-3 re-entry vehicle; Iran called documents 'forgeries and fabrications'

IAEA final assessment presented 15 Dec 2015: a range of activities relevant to developing a nuclear explosive device conducted before end of 2003 as a coordinated effort; some activities after 2003 'did not advance beyond feasibility and scientific studies'; 'no credible indications' of such activities after 2009; no diversion; Board closed the file
JCPOA: 3.67% cap for 15 years; 300 kg stockpile cap for 15 years; 5,060 IR-1 operating centrifuges for 10 years; Fordow converted, no uranium 15 years; Arak core removed
16 Apr 2021: Iran began enriching to 60% at Natanz after sabotage the previous week; Salehi: nine grams per hour

IAEA report (data as of 17 May 2025, public 31 May 2025): 408.6 kg of 60% HEU, up 133.8 kg; total enriched 9,247.6 kg; ~42 kg of 60% theoretically enough for one bomb if further enriched; Iran 'the only non-nuclear-weapon state' producing such material, 'serious concern'; Iran called report based on 'unreliable' sources; Netanyahu's office: Iran 'totally determined to complete its nuclear weapons program'

12 Jun 2025 IAEA Board found Iran in non-compliance 19-3-11 (Russia, China, Burkina Faso against), citing 'many failures' since 2019 and undeclared material at multiple locations; first in almost 20 years; Iran announced a new enrichment site and said resolution had 'no technical and legal basis'
Grossi to CNN (June 2025): 'we did not have any proof of a systematic effort to move into a nuclear weapon'

Khamenei's reported fatwa: oral ruling Oct 2003; cited by Iran at the IAEA Aug 2005 (production, stockpiling and use forbidden); 2010 message calling use 'haraam'; no published written text; Larijani 2025 said Iran would have 'no choice' if attacked; Khatib 2021 'cornered cat'
Lee Smith (2012): MEMRI searched Khamenei's sites and concluded 'No such fatwa ever existed or was ever published'; Juan Cole disputed this

March 2026: NPT withdrawal bill introduced 28 Mar 2026 by Malek Shariati; FM spokesman Baghaei: Iran 'has never sought, and does not seek, nuclear weapons'; no Article X notice; Iran submitted working papers to the 2026 RevCon
29 Sep 2026: Kremlin said it had no desire for Iran to leave the NPT; debate continuing; no formal withdrawal notice reported
Iran began enriching to 20% at Fordow in January 2012 (timeline); the Nov 2013 JPOA rolled back the 20% stockpile (ACA); before April 2021 Iran had again been enriching to 20% (AP)

ir4_dimona.topic: Israel's undeclared nuclear arsenal: Dimona, inspections, opacity, Vanunu, estimates, NPT resolutions

claims.text: France and Israel signed a revised agreement on 3 Oct 1957 for a 24 MWt reactor plus unwritten protocol for a reprocessing plant; Dimona built secretly outside IAEA inspection; US inspectors visited seven times in the 1960s; Israel controlled timing and agenda; reportedly false control panels and bricked-over passages; inspectors found no weapons activity; widely reported Israel had two bombs in 1967; late-1990s US IC estimate 75–130 weapons; FAS: possibly fewer than 100, claims of 400 exaggerated; Vanunu data implied ~40 kg plutonium a year

Vanunu abducted 30 Sep 1986 by agents of the Israeli government in Italy; Sunday Times published 5 Oct 1986; convicted of treason and aggravated espionage in camera; 18 years; held alone in Ashkelon; Israeli officials said in 1996 he could not be released for fear he would reveal secrets

Vanunu's disclosures led analysts to estimate 100–200 weapons; released 21 Apr 2004 after 18 years, more than 11 in solitary; barred from leaving Israel, contacts restricted; government feared further disclosures; Vanunu said he had none
SIPRI (June 2024): Israel ~90 warheads; upgrading Dimona plutonium facility; ~30 for aircraft, up to 50 for Jericho missiles, Dolphin submarines possibly; Israel neither confirms nor denies

UNGA A/RES/80/67, 1 Dec 2025: 145-6-30; no votes Argentina, Fiji, Israel, Micronesia, Palau, US; calls on Israel to join the NPT without further delay and place unsafeguarded facilities under full-scope IAEA safeguards
IAEA GC(53)/RES/17, 18 Sep 2009: 'calls upon Israel to accede to the NPT and place all its nuclear facilities under comprehensive IAEA safeguards'; 49-45-16 roll call
Sept 2010 resolution failed 51-46; Israel ties NPT accession to comprehensive regional peace; IAEC DG Shaul Chorev called Iran and Syria 'the real cases of dangerous proliferation and non-compliance'

Israel's 2018 explanation of vote rejected 'The Risk of Nuclear Proliferation in the Middle East' 'in its entirety', citing four regional states (Iran, Iraq, Syria, Libya) that 'violated their NPT obligations'
